entries.question: Who are you? What do you do? Tell me about you.
entries.answer:
I’m Yanwei Miao. I’m still trying to come up with a clever answer to this question. But for now, the important bit is that I’m a User Experience Designer, I’ve been doing this since 2017, and I genuinely love what I do!
[[file: YanweiMiao-UX.pdf | https://miaoyanwei.github.io/assets/YanweiMiao-UX.pdf]]
[[suggest: What's your educational background? | What's your professional experience?]]

entries.question: What do you know about design?
entries.answer: I have a good grounding in design principles and components, as well as psychology and behavioural theory. I take a user-centred approach to my work.

entries.question: Where are you based?
entries.answer: Currently I’m in Kolbermoor, a Kabuff in Bavaria near Apls. However, sometimes I run away from German winter for some vitamin D. Then you can find me in Shenzhen, Bangkok, or other sunnier places.

entries.question: What's your contact information?
entries.answer: E-mail me: myanwei@gmail.com, if you've got some business to talk about. Or follow me on my Instagram: @Miaoblabla, if you want to see some fun stuff.

entries.question: What's your weakness?
entries.answer: When I’m too excited, I sometimes want to dump all the ideas in my head at once, and I start talking a bit incoherently. Trust me, I’m just too excited and trying to express too many things in my second language at the same time. Which usually means I have a good bunch of exciting thoughts in my head. So please calm me down, or just give me a moment to organise myself. I’m usually quite self-aware of it.

entries.answer: Ach that lad is Stefan. Ask me something more useful please, Stefan.

entries.question: What languages do you speak?
entries.answer: I speak fluent English and Chinese, I also speak some German.

entries.question: What tools, techniques and technologies are you familiar with?
entries.answer:
I use a lot of tools for different purposes.
My best design and prototyping companion is Figma,
I also use Miro, Notion, etc. for brainstorming, planning, researching, and analysing.
I do simple coding tasks as well, mainly frontend technologies like HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
And like everybody else nowadays, I'm also a heavy user of LLMs, other than coding, I also use them for research, brainstorming, ideation, and sometimes design critics. They can be very good assistants.

entries.question: What is your educational background?
entries.answer:
I have a Master of Science in Human-Computer Interaction from the University of Siegen, another Master of Arts in Interaction Design from Loughborough University, and a Bachelor of Engineering in Industrial Design from Guangdong Ocean University. 
[[bubble]]
So, as you can probably tell, I have a pretty solid background in design.
[[suggest: Why designer?]]

entries.question: What have you been working on? What's your work experience?
entries.answer:
∙ Currently, I’m working as a UX designer at a Berlin start-up, where I’m helping build the Consenter ecosystem from 0 to 1.
∙ Before that, I worked in-house at a telecommunications company, leading the design of GlocalMe and its mobile applications.
∙ I’ve also worked on research and consultancy projects with organisations including Fraunhofer ISI, the Max Planck Institute for Meteorology, and Favorite Medium.
∙ Outside of work, I contribute to open-source projects, including Giraffe, a Figma plugin, Cow Defense, a small game project, and SmarterFAQ, an LLM-powered FAQ bot (which is what you’re talking to now).
[[suggest: Consenter | GlocalMe | FLEX | Pepper | Ableton | Autonomous Driving | Giraffe | Cow Defense | SmarterFAQ]]

entries.question: How is your work flow like?
entries.answer:
I always start with understanding the problem, the users and their needs. I usually spend a good time making the design goals clear before I actually drafting anything. This is, in my opinion, a very efficent way to come up with a thought through design, that actually avoids unnecessary iterations, which in the end will save a lot of time.
Then I'd like to design the interface within a user flow, this garantines a smooth and consistent experience.

entries.question: Why did you want to be a designer?
entries.answer:
I think I’ve always had some designer traits. I was pretty good at creative stuff when I was little. Before choosing my major at university, I actually went to a career consultancy. After going through a whole bunch of questions, my top career match was ✨designer. No joke. And if I remember correctly, journalist was second.
[[suggest: What designer traits do you have?]]

entries.question: What designer traits do you have?
entries.answer: 'Design is the art of creating order from chaos.' to be continue...

entries.question: What is the challenge or problem of being a UX designer? Why do you think you are a people pleaser?
entries.answer:
One challenge of being a UX designer is that we’re trained to be empathetic. We’re taught to be a good listener, understand people’s frustrations and needs, and avoid judging or dismissing their experiences. We try to see things from different perspectives so that we can design solutions that genuinely address users’ problems.
But I think that same quality can sometimes make designers vulnerable. When you’re used to listening, understanding, and trying to accommodate different perspectives, it can be difficult to separate empathy from taking on responsibilities that are not yours.
I’ve seen designers struggle with this, and I’m part of that group myself. I think one of the things we need to learn is how to stay empathetic and open while also maintaining professional boundaries. I’m still learning how to do that myself.

entries.question: What is Miao doing at Law & Innovation?
entries.answer: At Law & Innovation, Miao works on a novel product ecosystem from 0 to 1, including the Consenter ecosystem and related privacy and data-protection experiences.

entries.question: What is Consenter?
entries.answer: Consenter is a consent-management and privacy ecosystem intended to make digital consent more user-friendly while helping businesses and technology providers address privacy and compliance requirements.

entries.question: What was Miao's role in Consenter?
entries.answer: Miao is part of the PRD team at Law & Innovation and contributes to the design of the Consenter ecosystem, including experiences around consent, privacy and data protection.

entries.question: What is the Consent Agent?
entries.answer: The Consent Agent is a consumer-facing part of the Consenter ecosystem that allows people to give and manage consent across services and contexts.

entries.question: What problem does Consenter try to solve?
entries.answer: Consenter addresses the difficulty of making meaningful privacy and consent decisions in digital services, including the problem of consent fatigue and the tension between user expectations, data-driven services, businesses and regulators.

entries.question: What is Miao's previous industry experience?
entries.answer: Before Law & Innovation, Miao worked as an in-house designer at uCloudlink, a telecommunications company in Shenzhen.

entries.question: What did Miao do at uCloudlink?
entries.answer: At uCloudlink, Miao led the GlocalMe mobile applications and their derivatives and also gained hands-on experience with web and SaaS products.

entries.question: What is GlocalMe?
entries.answer: GlocalMe is a mobile connectivity service. Miao's portfolio describes the GlocalMe app as helping users buy data and manage devices to stay connected through GlocalMe mobile WiFi.

entries.question: What is Miao's experience with mobile apps?
entries.answer: Miao led the GlocalMe mobile applications and related products at uCloudlink and therefore has substantial experience designing mobile product experiences.

entries.question: Does Miao have web and SaaS experience?
entries.answer: Yes. Miao describes having hands-on experience with both web and SaaS products, in addition to mobile applications.

entries.question: What did Miao do at Fraunhofer ISI?
entries.answer: At Fraunhofer ISI, Miao developed a web tool providing personalised recommendations and explanations for optimising household energy systems.

entries.question: What was Miao's master's thesis about?
entries.answer: Miao's 2023 master's thesis at the University of Siegen was titled 'Filling the Information Gap: A Design Case Study of A Recommender for Home Energy System.' It explored the design of a recommender for household energy systems.

entries.question: What degree did Miao complete at the University of Siegen?
entries.answer: Miao completed a Master of Science in Human-Computer Interaction at the University of Siegen in 2023.

entries.question: What was the focus of Miao's HCI thesis?
entries.answer: The thesis focused on designing a recommender for home energy systems and on addressing information gaps between users and complex energy-system decisions.

entries.question: What did Miao do for the Max Planck Institute for Meteorology?
entries.answer: Miao consulted on user-centred design approaches for the high-performance computing team at the Max Planck Institute for Meteorology.

entries.question: What did Miao do for Ableton?
entries.answer: Miao worked with Favorite Medium to assess Ableton's checkout flows for APEC markets, identifying UX and cultural issues.

entries.question: What was the Ableton project about?
entries.answer: The Ableton project was a heuristic evaluation of the website checkout flow for APEC markets, with a focus on UX and cultural issues.

entries.question: Has Miao worked on international products?
entries.answer: Yes. Miao has worked on products and projects involving international markets, including Ableton's APEC checkout flows and GlocalMe products.

entries.question: What projects are shown in Miao's portfolio?
entries.answer: The portfolio currently highlights Consenter, GlocalMe, FLEX, a Pepper storytelling game, an Ableton checkout evaluation, and an autonomous-driving interaction project.

entries.question: What is the FLEX project?
entries.answer: FLEX is a design case study of a recommender for home energy systems, presented as 'Filling the information gap.'

entries.question: What is the Pepper project?
entries.answer:
The Pepper project, titled 'Erinnern Sie sich noch?', explored a storytelling game with the Pepper robot for memory training among older adults.
[Erinnern Sie sich noch? A Storytelling Game with Pepper for Older Adults' Memory Training](https://doi.org/10.48340/ihc2023_pd026)

entries.question: Was the Pepper project published?
entries.answer: Yes. 'Erinnern Sie sich noch? A Storytelling Game with Pepper for Older Adults' Memory Training' was published as a 2023 conference paper associated with EUSSET's InfraHEALTH conference.

entries.question: Who were Miao's co-authors on the Pepper project?
entries.answer: The published work lists Sofía González-Villalobos, Yanwei Miao, Julia Renardias and Mehrbod Manavi as authors.

entries.question: What was the goal of the Pepper storytelling game?
entries.answer: The project aimed to provide older adults with a meaningful memory-training activity while exploring how robot-based assistance could support nursing staff and caregivers.

entries.question: What is the autonomous-driving project?
entries.answer:
It is a student project developed in collaboration with Jaguar Land Rover in 2016 that explored how to enable trust in autonomous driving.
Here's a small video showing the interaction concept.
[[video: https://youtu.be/PbDz9k_xUNM?si=CJ2kQ43zCrSHH6GQ]]
[[file: Download Booklet.pdf | https://miaoyanwei.github.io/assets/jlr-booklet.pdf]]

entries.question: Did Miao work with Jaguar Land Rover?
entries.answer: Yes. The portfolio and LinkedIn profile describe an autonomous-driving project developed in collaboration with Jaguar Land Rover in 2016.

entries.question: What is Giraffe?
entries.answer: Giraffe is a Figma plugin that Miao is building with Raphael for exporting Figma frames as GIFs.

entries.question: What is Miao's role in Giraffe?
entries.answer: Miao describes being more focused on the design and creative side of Giraffe, while Raphael is the main coding contributor.

entries.question: What is Cow Defense?
entries.answer:
Cow Defense is a small tower defence game I’m building with Raphael. He’d always wanted to make an old-school game, and apparently thought my drawings were “simple yet charming” enough to invite me onto the project. So Raphael does the coding magic, while I take care of all the visual bits. Here’s a little sneak peek of what we’re building!
![Cow Defense](https://miaoyanwei.github.io/assets/cow-defense.gif)

entries.question: Does Miao contribute to open source?
entries.answer: Yes. Miao says they want to contribute to the open-source community and currently work on projects such as Giraffe and Cow Defense.

entries.question: What is Miaoblabla?
entries.answer: Miaoblabla is an Instagram account Miao manages to collect psychology and behaviourism theories that are relevant to designers.

entries.question: Why does Miao collect psychology and behaviourism theories for designers?
entries.answer: Miao's Miaoblabla project is intended to collect relevant psychology and behaviourism theories as an ongoing resource for designers.

entries.question: What design background does Miao have?
entries.answer: Miao describes having a solid background in design alongside more than six years of UX experience. Public portfolio material also shows work spanning industrial design, interaction design and HCI.

entries.question: What kind of products has Miao designed?
entries.answer: Miao has worked on mobile applications, web tools, SaaS products, consent and privacy services, energy-system recommenders, checkout experiences, robot interactions and autonomous-driving concepts.

entries.question: Has Miao worked on B2B products?
entries.answer: Yes. Miao has experience with web and SaaS products and currently works on a product ecosystem serving multiple stakeholder groups at Law & Innovation.

entries.question: Has Miao worked on B2C products?
entries.answer: Yes. Miao has designed consumer-facing experiences including GlocalMe mobile applications and consumer privacy and consent experiences within the Consenter ecosystem.

entries.question: Does Miao have research experience?
entries.answer: Yes. Miao's work includes HCI research, a master's thesis based on a design case study, user research around energy-system recommendations, and published work involving interaction with older adults and Pepper robots.

entries.question: Does Miao have user-centred design experience?
entries.answer: Yes. Miao has explicitly consulted on user-centred design approaches and has applied research and evaluation methods across product and HCI projects.

entries.question: What does Miao seem to value in UX design?
entries.answer: Miao's portfolio emphasises digital experiences that flow, user-centred approaches, understanding information gaps, trust in interaction, and making complex digital services easier to understand and use.

entries.question: What is Miao's approach to complex information?
entries.answer: A recurring theme in Miao's work is making complex information more understandable and actionable, as shown by the home-energy recommender and privacy and consent projects.

entries.question: What is Miao's approach to trust?
entries.answer: Trust is a recurring design theme in Miao's work, including the autonomous-driving project and the Consenter ecosystem, where understandable privacy and consent experiences are intended to support user confidence.

entries.question: What is Miao's connection to privacy UX?
entries.answer: Miao currently works on the Consenter ecosystem at Law & Innovation, which focuses on user-friendly privacy, consent and data-protection experiences.

entries.question: What is Miao's experience with legal and regulatory products?
entries.answer: At Law & Innovation, Miao works in a cross-disciplinary environment involving legal, technology and design and contributes UX/UI work to privacy and data-protection products.

entries.question: What kinds of teams has Miao worked with?
entries.answer: Miao has worked with multidisciplinary teams involving design, technology, legal, research and business stakeholders, including teams at Law & Innovation, uCloudlink, Fraunhofer ISI, Max Planck Institute for Meteorology and external consultancy collaborators.

entries.question: Has Miao worked in startups?
entries.answer: Yes. Miao currently works at Law & Innovation, a Berlin startup building a novel product ecosystem from 0 to 1.

entries.question: Has Miao worked in research institutions?
entries.answer: Yes. Miao has worked on projects involving Fraunhofer ISI, the Max Planck Institute for Meteorology and the University of Siegen.

entries.question: What makes Miao's background interdisciplinary?
entries.answer: Miao's experience combines product and UX design with HCI research, user-centred design, technology, privacy and data protection, and work across domains such as telecommunications, energy, healthcare-related interaction and autonomous driving.

entries.question: What are Miao's notable portfolio projects?
entries.answer: Notable projects include Consenter, GlocalMe, the FLEX home-energy recommender, the Pepper storytelling game, Ableton checkout evaluation, and an autonomous-driving interaction concept.

entries.question: What is Miao currently interested in?
entries.answer: Miao's current work centres on digital products, privacy and consent, while side projects explore design tools, games, psychology and behaviourism for designers.

entries.question: What does Miao do outside client or company work?
entries.answer: Miao works on open-source or side projects such as the Giraffe Figma plugin, Cow Defense game and Miaoblabla, an Instagram project about psychology and behaviourism for designers.

entries.question: What languages does Miao speak?
entries.answer: Miao's public LinkedIn profile lists Chinese as a native or bilingual language, English at a professional level, German at a basic level, and Cantonese as fluent.

entries.question: Where can I see Miao's portfolio?
entries.answer: Miao's portfolio is available at https://miaoyanwei.github.io/.

entries.question: What is Miao's professional profile in one sentence?
entries.answer: Miao is a UX designer with more than six years of experience who combines product design, HCI research and a multidisciplinary background to create digital experiences that flow.

entries.question: Why is Miao interested in UX?
entries.answer: Miao's portfolio shows a sustained interest in designing digital experiences that make complex information and interactions easier to understand, while creating value for both individuals and businesses.

entries.question: What types of problems does Miao enjoy solving?
entries.answer: Miao's portfolio suggests a particular interest in complex problems involving information gaps, trust, privacy, consent, user decision-making and the interaction between people and emerging technology.

entries.question: What is distinctive about Miao's portfolio?
entries.answer: The portfolio combines commercial product design with HCI research and experimental projects, spanning privacy, telecommunications, energy systems, social robotics, autonomous driving, design tools and games.
